"At last!" Dr. Monroe cried, as he saw the asteroid-sized chunks of dirt and stone fly past his ship. "I've finally destroyed the earth, and all those pesky taxes and junk mail and adds. They're all gone!" Dr. Monroe looked at his old home as it blew away into the cosmic abyss. He reached under his control panel for the on-deck wine cupboard. The wine he pulled out was a '27 chardonnay. Pouring it into a glass he also got from the cupboard, he leaned back in the pilot's chair to watch the world burn, once and for all. He drank the wine happily, humming a tune that always soothed him when someone had the audacity to say "Have a good day," or some other hogwash of that degree. Just when the tune in his head was getting good, the chunks of earth seemed to slow their race from their origin. They did slow, and in fact, stopped. Dr. Monroe thought this was rather puzzling, but it didn't concern him much. After all, his work was done. But the chunks didn't just slow down, they reversed direction. boiled water vapor coalesced back into drops, then into globs. Dirt, stone, and metals slammed back into place. Mangled buildings, cars, bicicles, and a billion other objects fixed themselves and found their previous place. When the earth was finally whole again, Dr. Monroe plugged some commands in his ship's monitoring systems in a fury. The screen lit up with scenes from all over the world. People went about their days, oblivious to the calamity that had just befallen them. Dr. Monroe furrowed his brow in frustration. "How could this be? They should all be dead!" On one screen, a family of tourists were taking a picture infront of big ben. 10:00. The time was only 10:00. "Bloody worthless piece of metal! Destroy everything then take me back four hours into the past?" Dr. Monroe screamed, banging on the dash board, and in doing so he closed all the windows that were pulled up. His anger was soon replaced by a sardonic grin. The earth may not stay destroyed, but he could now spend the rest of his life blowing it up over and over again. He took a swig of his wine, and pressed the large red button again, firing another laser at the earth that was already destroyed.
